Can you add to the Redfish.md?

Done, thanks!
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/6/docs/Redfish.md#1055
Is this documented in PDI ?
Thanks, will add PDI patch later.

Item.Memory interface definition is introduced in PDI change https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/89182 (linked in commit message). Item.Dimm (already in PDI) is matched in parallel for transition-period compatibility.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#214
Make sure that these redfish properties are not present when associated DBus interface is not present.

Addressed. In the new implementation, the destructor writes LifeTime only when both SRAM and DRAM MemoryECC interfaces are resolved successfully. EBADR / io_error on either side is treated as "interface not present" and LifeTime is omitted entirely (no default zero).

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#55
This comment seems redundant because it doesn’t add anything beyond what can already be inferred from the function parameter names. Same applies to other comments in this file.

Removed redundant comments. Only kept control-flow notes that explain non-obvious branches.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp

Instead of doing this in bmcweb, sensor daemon should ideally be exposing correct ECC Error Count by doing sram + dram. It would simplify bmcweb logic quite a bit. In this case dbus-sensors can directly publish the sram + dram value here - https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/87166/34/src/nvidia-gpu/NvidiaGpuMemoryDevice.cpp#132.

After discussion with you, decided to keep the current approach. Thanks.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#55
nit: this doesn't need to be separate function in my opinion.

Agreed. The original findProcessorMemoryObject wrapper was removed in PS16. The structure was refactored to use a shared accumulator with std::bind_front callbacks, so the remaining named functions (here: afterGetDramEccService) are the actual callback bodies, not thin wrappers over a single D-Bus call.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#112
For errors other than boost::system::errc::io_error or EBADR, we should log error report messages::internalError.

Fixed. Non-EBADR / non-io_error branches now BMCWEB_LOG_ERROR and set acc->hasError = true; the shared accumulator destructor emits messages::internalError. Applied consistently across all five callbacks.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#82
nit: this doesn't need to be separate function in my opinion.

Agreed. The original getProcessorMemorySummarySramEcc wrapper was removed in PS16. The structure was refactored to use a shared accumulator with std::bind_front callbacks, so the remaining named functions (here: afterGetDramAssociation) are the actual callback bodies, not thin wrappers over a single D-Bus call.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#144
For errors other than boost::system::errc::io_error or EBADR, we should log error report messages::internalError.

Fixed — see reply on L193. Same EBADR / io_error vs. other-error split applied here.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#183
We should log error and return messages::internalError if multiple services are found.

Fixed. object.size() != 1 now logs an error identifying the path and sets acc->hasError = true; destructor returns messages::internalError.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#132
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#245
nit: this doesn't need to be separate function in my opinion.

Agreed. The original getProcessorMemorySummaryMetricsData wrapper was removed in PS16. The structure was refactored to use a shared accumulator with std::bind_front callbacks, so the remaining named functions (here: afterGetSramEccService) are the actual callback bodies, not thin wrappers over a single D-Bus call.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#224
Can't we use getProcessorObject from processor.hpp?

Done. handleProcessorMemorySummaryMetricsGet now uses getProcessorObject from processor.hpp to resolve the processor D-Bus path, then chains SRAM + DRAM queries through a shared accumulator.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#323
use std::format.

Done. Name field now built with std::format("{} Memory Summary Metrics", processorId).

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/16/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#321
We need to simply logic here to make code more readable. See if using only one variable instead of three is feasible.
Why is it mandatory that both should be present? Shouldn't we populate these properties even if one of them is found?
Please use getAssociatedSubTree to avoid subsequent DBus method call to get the service.
Let's not manually invoke a function that is meant to be a callback. Separate out some of part of afterGetSramEccProperties in separate function and call it here.
Why do we need a new DBus method call to get the service? can't we use lamda parameter `serviceMap`.

Done in PS20. Accumulator: 3 bools + 4 counters -> 2 bools (hasAnyEcc/hasError) + 1 ce/ueCount pair. Per-source counters merged because output sums them; presence and error stay separate (orthogonal).

Diff: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/18..20/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#60

Done in PS20. Dropped the both-required check. LifeTime emitted when SRAM or DRAM yields data; omitted entirely when neither is reachable (Redfish absent-property convention).

Diff: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/18..20/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#75
Shouldn't this be continue?

We can't do this. Either we have to add interface `xyz.openbmc_project.Memory.MemoryECC` to getAssociatedSubTree call and report error if more than one service is found OR iterate over all services to find the one containing `xyz.openbmc_project.Memory.MemoryECC`.
Can we also add xyz.openbmc_project.Memory.MemoryECC interface to this list?

Done in PS20. Switched to getAssociatedSubTree -> path + serviceMap in one call. Service taken via serviceMap.begin()->first; getDbusObject removed.

Diff: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/18..20/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#176 (call), https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/18..20/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#161 (service)

Done in PS20. Extracted startDramAssociationProbe(). SRAM-success and SRAM-absent paths both call it directly; no more forged error_code into afterGetSramEccProperties.

Diff: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/18..20/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#168 (helper), https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/18..20/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#197 (absent path), https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/18..20/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#218 (success path)
If serviceMap is empty, does that mean there is no Processor Object path? If yes, shouldn't we return `resource not found`?
we have to iterate over all services to find the one containing `xyz.openbmc_project.Memory.MemoryECC`.

Done in PS20. Lambda reads service from getProcessorObject's serviceMap parameter directly; getDbusObject removed. Empty serviceMap falls through to startDramAssociationProbe to keep accumulator lifecycle intact.

Diff: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/18..20/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#284 (service), https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/18..20/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#274 (fallback)

Done. Changed return to continue so a single failing DRAM path no longer aborts the whole accumulator (matches the partial-data-preferred intent).

PS23 line: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/23/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#164

Done. Took both options:
- Added Memory.MemoryECC to memoryInterfaces so the mapper pre-filters paths exposing the ECC interface.
- Iterate serviceMap with std::ranges::find_if to find the entry hosting MemoryECC; serviceMap.begin()->first is unsafe because a path can be served by multiple services.

PS23 line: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/23/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#156

Done. memoryInterfaces is now {Item.Dimm, Memory.MemoryECC}; mapper pre-filters paths that expose MemoryECC.

PS23 line: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/23/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#177

Done. Empty serviceMap from getProcessorObject now returns messages::resourceNotFound("Processor", processorId) instead of silently falling through to the DRAM-only probe.

PS23 line: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/23/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#279

Done. Iterate serviceMap with std::ranges::find_if to find the entry hosting Memory.MemoryECC instead of taking begin()->first; same pattern as the DRAM lookup.

PS23 line: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87185/23/redfish-core/lib/processor_memory_summary_metrics.hpp#290
Could we add a `bmcweb:` ?
Rename to Memory, done, thanks
please use sdbusplus::object_path
Done, thanks.
please use sdbusplus::object_path
Done, thanks.

This lambda is ~20 lines, exceeding COMMON_ERRORS.md §14 (<10 lines).
Suggest extracting afterGetProcessorObjectForMemorySummary and binding via std::bind_front.
https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/docs/COMMON_ERRORS.md#14-very-long-lambda-callbacks
Done, thanks.
